tagline: The fish that looks up through its own forehead
summary: A small twilight-zone fish whose glowing green, tube-shaped eyes sit inside a transparent, fluid-filled shield on its head. It hovers almost motionless, scanning the faint light above for the silhouettes of prey, then rotates its eyes forward to feed.
ability: rotating tubular eyes inside a see-through head

stats.range: North Pacific, from the Bering Sea to Japan and Baja California
stats.diet: Zooplankton, including small crustaceans and siphonophores

facts.title: A see-through head
facts.text: A transparent, fluid-filled shield covers the top of the head. It was missing from most older descriptions, probably because the fragile dome was destroyed when fish were hauled up in nets.

facts.title: Eyes that swivel
facts.text: Its tubular eyes were long thought to be fixed, staring only upward. Robison and Reisenbichler (2008) used ROV video and a live, net-caught fish to show the eyes rotate forward as the fish tilts to feed.

facts.title: Green sunglasses
facts.text: The tubular eyes are capped by bright green lenses. MBARI suggests the green pigment filters out direct sunlight, helping the fish pick out the bioluminescent glow of prey overhead.

facts.title: Hovering hunter
facts.text: Large, flat fins let it hang nearly motionless and manoeuvre precisely. Its pointed mouth is small, but its gut is large, and two net-caught fish had jelly fragments in their stomachs.

facts.title: Thief among tentacles?
facts.text: Researchers speculate it may pick prey out of the stinging tentacles of siphonophores (colonial jellies), with its clear shield protecting its eyes from stings — an idea still to be confirmed.

references.title: Researchers solve mystery of deep-sea fish with tubular eyes and transparent head
Robison, B.H. & Reisenbichler, K.R. (2008). Macropinna microstoma and the paradox of its tubular eyes. Copeia 2008(4): 780–784

image.alt: A small black fish lying on an open palm; the front of its head is a clear dome through which a large dark eye is visible.
image.caption: A barreleye collected by trawl in the Gulf of Alaska during a NOAA Ocean Exploration expedition; its clear head shield is still intact.
image.creator: NOAA Ocean Exploration, Exploring Pelagic Biodiversity of the Gulf of Alaska and the Impact of Its Seamounts (author not named)

notes: Only one licence-compatible Commons image of M. microstoma exists (fresh trawl specimen held in a hand, NOAA public domain; Commons file description says 'a barreleye fish (Opisthoproctidae)' but it is filed in Category:Macropinna microstoma and the transparent head shield and tubular eyes match). MBARI's in-situ ROV images are copyrighted. 'Barreleye' is also used for other Opisthoproctidae. Conservation status per FishBase (IUCN Not Evaluated). WoRMS places the family in Argentiniformes; class given as Teleostei per WoRMS.
